text:
sarah.g: FYI customer 'AcmeHealth' opened an escalation — after we enabled AWS PrivateLink for their account their API calls intermittently 502 or TLS handshake fails when routed through interface endpoints. Happening ~30% of requests, no change on our side.

customer-acme: seeing: 
  curl -v https://api.redwood.example.com/generate 
  * Connected to vpce-0abc1234-xxxx.subnet-b.vpce.amazonaws.com (10.10.2.45) port 443 (#0)
  * TLS handshake: SSL connection error
  * Closing connection 0
  curl: (35) error:14094438:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert protocol version

ben.i: thanks. do we have a repro with tcpdump or ALB logs?

customer-acme: attached a pcap and traceroute. traceroute shows jumps between AZs, sometimes 10.10.2.45 doesn't accept, then request goes to 10.10.1.12 and succeeds.

leo.oncall: quick checklist: private DNS enabled on interface endpoint? SG rules allow outbound 443 to our service? NACLs? source/dest-check on instances?

sarah.g: customer confirms private dns = enabled. SG on endpoint is pretty tight — only allows outbound to 0.0.0.0/0:443 blocked, they have a specific egress allowlist to a NAT GW IP range.

ben.i: ah. endpoint ENIs are in multiple AZ subnets, but their egress policy/NAT layout is single-AZ NAT. If an ENI lands in an AZ where subnet route table points to a blackhole or to a NAT with no egress to our IP ranges, TLS will fail intermittently.

infra-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-0421-PrivLinkRoute. Tagging eng-infra.

leo.oncall: can customer run this to show which ENI responds per attempt? 
  for i in {1..20}; do date +%s; curl -sSv -o /dev/null -w "%{remote_ip} %{http_code}\n" https://api.redwood.example.com/generate; sleep 0.5; done

customer-acme: ran it, output: 
  10.10.2.45 000
  10.10.1.12 200
  10.10.2.45 000
  10.10.3.22 000
  10.10.1.12 200

ben.i: so 10.10.1.12 is the only ENI that can egress to our public IPs. The others probably route to their NAT that doesn't permit outbound to our endpoints or to egress proxy with TLS intercept?

sarah.g: customer also has an egress proxy that does TLS MITM for inspection. That would break SNI/certs for our endpoint, causing TLS alerts. But why only some ENIs? because only some subnets route traffic through the proxy. Mixed routing config.

leo.oncall: recommended next steps for customer:
- identify subnets used by interface endpoint ENIs (describe-network-interfaces on EC2 console).
- ensure those subnets' route tables have a valid default route to NAT or IGW that allows outbound to our IP ranges (or to their proxy if it preserves SNI).
- check endpoint security group: allow outbound 443 to our service IP ranges or 0.0.0.0/0 temporarily to test.
- If using Private DNS + Route53 Resolver rules, ensure there are no conflicting inbound endpoints or split-horizon rules that direct api.redwood.example.com to wrong IPs.

ben.i: adding commands: 
  # list ENIs for the endpoint
  aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters Name=description,Values="*vpce-0abc1234*" --query 'NetworkInterfaces[*].{Subnet:SubnetId,PrivateIp:PrivateIpAddress,AZ:AvailabilityZone}' --output table

  # show route table for subnet X
  aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=association.subnet-id,Values=subnet-0a1b2c3d --query 'RouteTables[0].Routes' --output json

sarah.g: customer ran the ENI list and route check. Results: ENI in subnet-0a in AZ a -> route to nat-0a (which is in a different account and has strict egress ACL). subnet-0b -> route to nat-0b (working). subnet-0c -> local only (no default route).

customer-acme: we had assumed interface endpoints would always be able to reach our service. Seems wrong. Is there a best practice?

leo.oncall: best practice: place interface endpoint ENIs in subnets that have consistent egress to the internet or to a proxy that preserves TLS. If you want consistent behavior, use dedicated subnets with known NAT or route to a centralized egress that allows our IPs. Also consider enabling endpoint-specific SG that allows outbound 443 so ENIs can connect directly without hitting egress proxies.

ben.i: also check AWS PrivateLink private DNS behavior: if you have split-horizon Route53 resolver rules or inbound endpoints, DNS resolution might return different private IPs across AZs. Verify Route53 "private hosted zone" doesn't conflict.

customer-acme: we updated route table for subnet-0c to point to nat-0b and relaxed SG on ENI to allow ephemeral outbound to 0.0.0.0/0:443 for test. After that errors dropped to <1%.

sarah.g: great. next steps:
- customer to keep relaxed SG for 24h to verify.
- if stable, recommend locking SG to our published egress IP ranges or moving ENIs into subnets that already have approved egress.
- infra to produce a short KB for customers about mixed-AZ NAT + PrivateLink gotchas.

leo.oncall: I can draft KB. Also pinging eng-runtime to confirm we can publish a clear list of IPs and ports customers should allow for PrivateLink egress. @ben.i want to follow on policy implications for PrivateLink endpoint policy?

ben.i: yes. I'll forward the trace and pcap to eng-sre for deeper packet analysis in case there's subtle TLS interception issues.

sarah.g: marking thread as customer-acknowledged. If they re-open we'll escalate. Thanks all :thumbsup:

customer-acme: thanks team — fixing route tables reduced errors, will monitor and update in 12h. Appreciate the quick help.
